stage_state.summary_md:
# Statistical and Psychometric Foundations

The methodology relies on established psychometric and statistical frameworks. Foundational texts include J. C. Nunnally’s *Psychometric Theory* (1978) and Timothy A. Brown’s *Confirmatory Factor Analysis for Applied Research* (2006). The authors utilize Partial Least Squares (PLS) analysis, drawing on Wynne W. Chin’s guidelines for reporting PLS analyses (2010) and Gefen and Straub’s guide to factorial validity (2005). Multivariate techniques are grounded in Hair et al.’s *Multivariate Data Analysis* (2006) and Ward’s hierarchical grouping methods (1963).

# Organizational Culture and Leadership

Organizational culture is anchored by Ron Westrum’s "A Typology of Organisational Cultures" (2004) and E. H. Schein’s *Organizational Culture and Leadership* (1985). Leadership models are informed by Rafferty and Griffin’s dimensions of transformational leadership (2004) and Stone, Russell, and Patterson’s comparison of transformational and servant leadership (2004). Cultural transformation is contextualized through John Shook’s analysis of NUMMI (2010).

# Diversity, Burnout, and Psychology

Diversity's impact is supported by Woolley and Malone’s "What Makes a Team Smarter? More Women" (2011) and Hunt, Layton, and Prince’s "Why Diversity Matters" (2015). The attrition of women in tech is examined through Kieran Snyder’s finding that culture drives women away (2014) and Leslie et al.’s research on expectations of brilliance (2015). Burnout and stress are analyzed using Leiter and Maslach’s predictors of job burnout (2008) and Chandola et al.’s study on chronic stress (2006).

# IT Performance and Business Value

The debate on technology's business value contrasts Nicholas G. Carr’s "IT Doesn’t Matter" (2003) with McAfee and Brynjolfsson’s "Investing in the IT That Makes a Competitive Difference" (2008). Software delivery practices are grounded in Beck et al.’s "Manifesto for Agile Software" (2001) and Humble and Farley’s *Continuous Delivery* (2010).
